title: Trees to Offset a Flight: CO₂ Calculator + Route Table | Hacé Cuentas
h1: How Many Trees Do You Need to Offset Your Flight's CO₂?
description: Calculate how many trees you need to offset your flight's CO₂ emissions. Enter distance and cabin class — get the answer instantly. Includes route table and ICAO emission factors for 2026.
answerSnippet: A young tree absorbs about 22 kg of CO₂ per year (USDA Forest Service). A 10,000 km economy-class flight emits ~1,500 kg CO₂, requiring 68 trees planted and grown for 1 year to offset it. Formula: trees = (km × emission factor) ÷ 22. Economy factor: 0.15 kg/km; business: 0.45 kg/km.
intro: Flying is one of the highest-impact activities for your personal carbon footprint. A single long-haul economy flight emits approximately 0.15 kg of CO₂ per kilometer per passenger (ICAO 2023 methodology), while business class produces roughly 3× more due to the extra seat space occupied. This calculator uses the ICAO emission factors and the USDA Forest Service standard of 22 kg CO₂ absorbed per young tree per year to tell you exactly how many trees you need to offset your trip.
keyTakeaway: Formula: **trees = (km × class factor) ÷ 22 kg CO₂/tree/year**. Economy factor = 0.15 kg/km; business = 0.45 kg/km. A Buenos Aires–Madrid flight (10,000 km, economy) requires planting 68 trees maintained for 1 year.

example.title: Worked example
steps: Buenos Aires → Madrid (10,000 km), economy class
example.result: Plant and maintain 68 trees for 1 year to offset this intercontinental flight

explanation:
## How the calculation works

The offset is computed in two steps:

1. **Flight CO₂** = distance × cabin class emission factor
   - Economy: 0.15 kg CO₂/passenger-km (ICAO 2023)
   - Premium economy: 0.24 kg/passenger-km
   - Business: 0.45 kg/passenger-km (3× economy, larger seat footprint)
   - First: 0.60 kg/passenger-km
2. **Trees needed** = total CO₂ ÷ 22 kg/year (USDA Forest Service average annual absorption for a young tree aged 0–20 years)

## Common routes: CO₂ and trees needed

| Route | Distance (one way) | CO₂ economy | Trees (economy) | CO₂ business | Trees (business) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New York — Los Angeles | 3,940 km | 591 kg | 27 | 1,773 kg | 81 |
| London — New York | 5,540 km | 831 kg | 38 | 2,493 kg | 114 |
| London — Dubai | 5,490 km | 824 kg | 38 | 2,471 kg | 113 |
| New York — Paris | 5,840 km | 876 kg | 40 | 2,628 kg | 120 |
| Sydney — Singapore | 6,310 km | 947 kg | 44 | 2,840 kg | 129 |
| Los Angeles — Tokyo | 8,770 km | 1,316 kg | 60 | 3,947 kg | 180 |
| Buenos Aires — Madrid | 10,000 km | 1,500 kg | 68 | 4,500 kg | 205 |
| Sydney — London | 16,900 km | 2,535 kg | 116 | 7,605 kg | 346 |

## Tree CO₂ absorption reference

| Tree type | CO₂ absorbed/year |
|---|---|
| Young tree (0–20 years) | 22 kg |
| Mature tree (20–50 years) | 45–60 kg |
| Large old-growth tree | 80–100 kg |
| Native forest per hectare | 5–10 tonnes |

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting radiative forcing**: At cruising altitude, nitrogen oxides, condensation trails, and cirrus clouds multiply the total climate effect by ~1.9× compared to CO₂ alone (Lee et al., 2021). This calculator shows the CO₂ base; for total climate impact, multiply by 1.9.
- **Not doubling for a round trip**: A round-trip flight is twice the one-way distance. A New York–London return is ~11,080 km, not 5,540.
- **Assuming one tree fixes it immediately**: Trees absorb CO₂ gradually over decades. The 22 kg/year figure means trees must grow for years — planting 68 trees offsets the flight in one year, or 1 tree offsets it in 68 years.
- **Trusting uncertified offset programs**: Only Gold Standard, Verra (VCS), and Climate Action Reserve have externally audited methodologies. A 2023 Guardian/Die Zeit investigation found >90% of Verra's forest credits generated no real emission reductions.

## Related calculators

- [Total carbon footprint tree offset](/calculadora-arboles-compensar-co2-huella)
- [CO₂ saved by unplugging chargers](/calculadora-ahorro-co2-cargador-desenchufar)

faq.q: How many trees does it take to offset a flight from New York to London?
faq.a: The New York–London route is about 5,540 km one way. In economy class (0.15 kg CO₂/km) that's 831 kg of CO₂, requiring 38 trees grown for 1 year to offset it. In business class (0.45 kg/km) it's 2,493 kg — needing 114 trees.

The ICAO standard assigns an emission factor per cabin class per kilometer: economy = 0.15 kg CO₂/km, premium economy = 0.24 kg/km, business = 0.45 kg/km, first = 0.60 kg/km. Multiply that by the flight distance to get total CO₂ per passenger.

faq.q: Why 22 kg of CO₂ per tree per year?
faq.a: This is the USDA Forest Service average for a young, healthy tree (ages 0–20) in a temperate climate. Mature trees absorb more (45–60 kg/year); saplings absorb less. It is the standard reference used in carbon offset calculations worldwide.

faq.q: How long does it take one tree to offset a long-haul flight?
faq.a: A transatlantic flight emitting 1,500 kg would take a single young tree about 68 years (1,500 ÷ 22) to offset. That is why meaningful compensation requires planting many trees, not just one.

faq.q: What is radiative forcing and why does it matter for flying?
faq.a: At 10,000 m altitude, contrails, cirrus clouds, and nitrogen oxides amplify the climate impact of aviation by roughly 1.9× compared to CO₂ alone (Lee et al., 2021, Atmospheric Environment). This calculator shows only the CO₂ component; for the full climate impact, multiply the result by 1.9.

faq.q: Is economy class really more eco-friendly than business?
faq.a: Yes — economy passengers emit roughly 3× less CO₂ per person than business-class passengers on the same flight because more people share the same seat space. Direct routes also help: takeoff and landing consume up to 25% of total fuel, so connecting flights are significantly worse.

faq.q: Are airline carbon offset programs trustworthy?
faq.a: Many are not. Only programs certified by Gold Standard, Verra (VCS), or Climate Action Reserve have externally audited methodology. A 2023 investigation by The Guardian and Die Zeit found that over 90% of Verra's forest offset credits did not represent real emission reductions. Always verify the certification before buying an offset.

faq.q: Can I donate money instead of physically planting trees?
faq.a: Yes. Organizations like Eden Reforestation Projects, One Tree Planted, and Plant-for-the-Planet plant trees for USD 1–5 each with on-the-ground verification. Offsetting 68 trees (one long-haul flight) costs roughly USD 70–340 depending on the program.

faq.q: Does this calculator count the return flight?
faq.a: No — enter only the distance you want to calculate. For a round trip, enter double the one-way distance (e.g., New York–London return = 11,080 km, not 5,540).

faq.q: Do native tree species absorb more CO₂?
faq.a: Not necessarily more per tree, but more sustainably. Native species maintain biodiversity and resist local pests and disease. Monoculture plantations (e.g., eucalyptus in tropical zones) often fail within 10 years, wiping out the offset benefit.
